headline: Agent-security attack success rates lack a shared measurement contract
summary: An arXiv preprint analyzes 259 papers reporting agentic-security attack success rates from a query-retrieved English-language arXiv corpus. The authors report that 58.0% of a seeded hand-coded sample of 50 papers (95% Wilson CI 44.2–70.6) reported neither a variance estimate nor repeated runs; revised automated detectors estimate 65.3% across all 259. They identify six choices that can change what an ASR measures, including evaluation unit, success oracle, attacker adaptivity, and defense knowledge. The paper argues these differences can make cross-paper values incomparable. It does not claim any individual paper is wrong, and its ranking-reversal estimates are analytical rather than observed defense comparisons.
